sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea (Language and Linguistics Monograph Series). Taipei: Academia Sinica. Front matter incl. Table 0.1 'Approximate number of contact hours with languages of the Admiralties'.
sources.note: Elu is not among the 26 Admiralty languages Blust recorded in 1975 (Table 0.1), so there is no Blust sketch or field-notebook packet for Elu; Kaipuleohone search 'Blust Elu' returns nothing relevant.

sources.citation: [SIL PNG] Kurti Organised Phonology Data (data checked by Bob Uebele, 2002; archived 2011). NEAREST RELATIVE ONLY (Kurti, kurt1250), not Elu.
sources.note: For Kurti (Elu's closest relative per Schooling 1988 and Glottolog's Kurti-Elu node), p.3: 'Stress in Kurti is non-contrastive, and is always on the final syllable of the word.' Not a statement about Elu; noted for context only.

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives search for ISO [elu] and SIL-PNG 'Languages of Papua New Guinea' resources index for code elu (fetched sources 2026-09-17 with headful Chrome; Cloudflare blocks curl).
sources.note: '0 items found' (sil.org) and 'No results found' (pnglanguages.sil.org): no Organised Phonology Data, phonology essentials, dialect or sociolinguistic survey exists for Elu in the SIL archive.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98 (ch. 9 'The Admiralties cluster'); Smythe, W.E. 1970. Melanesian, Micronesian, and Indonesian features in languages of the Admiralty Islands. PL C-13: 1209-1234; Lynch, Ross & Crowley 2002. The Oceanic Languages (listing p.879); Blust 1996 PL C-133; Blust 2013 The Austronesian Languages.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: None of these mentions Elu beyond a name in an index/speaker table (Blust 2013 p.100); Ross 1988, Smythe 1970, Blust 1996 and the LRC 2002 East Manus listing do not include Elu at all. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Schooling, Stephen & Janice Schooling. 1988. A preliminary sociolinguistic and linguistic survey of Manus Province, Papua New Guinea. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26, 211-241. Pacific Linguistics A-76. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Elu appears only at p.222 sec. 3.3 item 6 'Kurti and Elu' (spoken near Lowa, closely related to Kurti), in village lists (Kareng, Lowa, Mariman) and the cognate chart (pop. 216). Sec. 3.4 'Brief grammatical notes' gives pan-Manus characteristic consonants/vowels only; the words stress/accent/tone do not occur.

sources.citation: Healey, Alan. 1976. Austronesian languages: Admiralty Islands area. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2, 349-364. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Elu appears only in Figure 1 'Meyer's classification' (p.352, eastern Manus column); the chapter is classification/history only.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid eluu1241 and subgroup kurt1252 (Kurti-Elu); Ethnologue free page elu; Grokipedia 'Elu language (Papua New Guinea)'; OLAC language/elu (JS app, only Ethnologue entry per search snippet); PARADISEC/ELCat probes.
sources.note: Glottolog's only descriptive reference is Schooling & Schooling 1988 (overview). Grokipedia itself states Elu phonology 'is not comprehensively described in published sources'. No stress information anywhere.
